wrappedTokenCreation.notes: The Wormhole TypeScript SDK's own submitAttestation() wrapper reverted (both on Fuji and initially on Sepolia) -- root-caused and worked around by calling createWrapped(bytes) directly via ethers using the VAA the SDK itself fetched. The VAA and the destination contract were both fine; the SDK's transaction-construction wrapper was the actual problem.

realTransfer.status: COMPLETE -- real, end-to-end, verified. A user's $INAYA was locked on BSC Testnet and the equivalent wrapped $INAYA is confirmed present in their wallet on Sepolia.

correctedBug.description: A first attempt targeted Wormhole chain ID 2 ('Ethereum', mainnet's ID) instead of 10002 ('Sepolia', the actual testnet-specific ID) -- Wormhole registers Sepolia as its own distinct chain, separate from mainnet Ethereum, unlike BSC/Avalanche which have a single mainnet-name-covers-testnet-too mapping. That attempt's completeTransfer() reverted on-chain with InvalidTargetChain() (selector 0x376f6e4a, confirmed by computing keccak256 selectors for every custom error in Wormhole's Bridge.sol and matching). The stray locked amount from that attempt (tx 0x982d65f2e7e8c8142a8a23452f3d71d7149e0c38cc99c78f4922df91feef9c96) is inert -- its VAA targets chain 2, which nothing here will ever submit to. Fixed in src/lib/chain-adapters/interop/WormholeProvider.js's chain-name mapping, which had the identical bug for Ethereum/Arbitrum/Base/Optimism (Polygon has no fix -- Wormhole genuinely doesn't cover Inaya's Amoy target, see that file's comment).
correctedBug.realTransferTx: See realTransfer above for the corrected, successful attempt.
